comments.body: Landed as Gerrit change 3099, commit ed501817343, LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with no advisories. Root cause recorded in the description: 15 shell launches use the literal /bin/sh, which Windows resolves as drive-relative \bin\sh (WinError 2 in Windows sweep run 35572919806). The guard is a module-level skipif on /bin/sh being executable. A scratch copy pointed at a nonexistent path reported 15 skipped with the reason; on this host all 15 pass. make verify locally: only the 17 known pandoc failures under tests/unit/reconciler. The Windows sweep effect is tracked in the linked P4 task.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Every one of the **15** tests in `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` fails on the Windows
advisory sweep with `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file
specified`. The file exercises `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` by invoking it as a shell
script; Windows runners have no such interpreter on PATH, so the subprocess launch fails
before any assertion is reached.

The module carries **no** platform guard. `grep -nE "skipif|os.name|platform|sys.platform"
tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` returns nothing.

## Evidence

Sweep run `35572919806`, job `106248614492` (`sweep (windows)`) at `1b3bf5ffd1f`:

```
$ grep -c "FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py" win.log
15
$ grep -c "^def test_" tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py
15
```

15 of 15. Sample failures:

```
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_with_dir_lock_uses_python_fcntl_when_flock_binary_unavailable - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_with_dir_lock_serializes_concurrent_holders - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
FAILED tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py::test_clean_code_workspace_behind_origin_main_fast_forwards - FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
```

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

These are not 15 distinct defects. They are one environmental precondition reported 15 times,
and they inflate the Windows failure count without carrying any signal — the same erosion
`6798-606d-...` describes at the whole-lane level. A skip carries the true information ("this
suite requires a POSIX shell") where a failure asserts something false ("the entrypoint is
broken").

The class is also **growing**. `5967-b043-0a4e-4971`'s fix added 2 tests to this module
(`test_with_dir_lock_uses_python_fcntl_when_flock_binary_unavailable` and
`test_with_dir_lock_reports_unavailable_mechanism_not_timeout`), which immediately joined the
failing set. Any future work on the entrypoint enlarges it further, so the guard should land
before the next addition rather than after.

## Root cause (checked 2026-10-24)
The module launches `/bin/sh` by absolute path at every shell call site (about 15 in `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py`, for example the `["/bin/sh", str(_ENTRYPOINT), "--provision-only"]` call). Windows has no `/bin/sh`: `ntpath` treats it as the drive-relative path `\bin\sh`, which `CreateProcess` cannot find, and the Windows sweep log (run 35572919806) shows `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]` from those launches. It is the interpreter path, not translation of the script path. A `PATH` lookup would be the wrong guard: Git for Windows puts `sh` on `PATH`, but the tests would still fail on the literal `/bin/sh`.

## Approach
Add a module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not os.access("/bin/sh", os.X_OK), reason=...)` to `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py`. It keys on the capability the tests actually need (an executable `/bin/sh`), not on `os.name`, and the reason names that capability. No test body, helper or fixture changes.

## Scope
In scope: `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` only. Out of scope: making the entrypoint tests run on Windows, and the other Windows sweep failure classes (`6798-606d`).

## Testing
```
pytest tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py -q
make verify
```
The skip is exercised by evaluating the identical marker expression against a path that does not exist, in a scratch test, and checking pytest reports 15 skipped with the reason. Failure case: with `/bin/sh` absent the module must report skips, not errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The cause is recorded: every shell launch uses the literal `/bin/sh`, which Windows cannot resolve (checked: grep of the module plus the Windows sweep log line, recorded in a ticket comment).
- [x] `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` skips instead of failing when `/bin/sh` is not executable (checked: scratch test with a nonexistent path reports 15 skipped).
- [x] The guard tests the capability, not `os.name` or `sys.platform` (checked: review of the diff).
- [x] The skip reason names the missing `/bin/sh` (checked: pytest `-rs` output).
- [x] All 15 tests still run and pass on Linux and macOS (checked: `pytest tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py -q` shows 15 passed).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).

## Follow-up
A Windows sweep reporting 15 skips instead of 15 failures needs a future sweep run, so it is tracked in its own ticket rather than held open here.
